title: Nasdaq Soars to Record High as AI Frenzy Accelerates, Wall Street Celebrates】
body:
Wall Street’s Nasdaq Composite surged to a fresh all‑time high on Tuesday, propelled by a wave of optimism surrounding artificial‑intelligence (AI) stocks despite lingering worries about the technology’s safety, soaring valuations and the geopolitical shock of the United States’ escalating conflict with Iran. The benchmark index closed at 15,432.68 points, eclipsing its previous record set last month and underscoring the market’s willingness to overlook macro‑risk factors in favor of growth‑driven earnings narratives.

The rally was led by a cluster of AI‑focused companies that have become the centerpiece of investor attention since the release of powerful large‑language models earlier this year. Chipmakers such as Nvidia (NVDA) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) posted double‑digit gains, while cloud‑service providers and software firms that tout AI‑enhanced offerings also posted robust advances. Nvidia, the market’s biggest beneficiary, added more than 5 % to its share price, pushing its market capitalization past the $1.4 trillion threshold for the first time. Analysts attribute the surge to expectations that AI will drive a new wave of hardware demand, from data‑center GPUs to specialized inference chips, and that the technology will become a core revenue pillar for a broader swath of the tech sector.

Even as the AI euphoria builds, investors appear to be discounting a set of countervailing concerns that have haunted the market in recent weeks. The United States’ recent missile strikes on Iranian targets have sparked a spike in oil prices, with Brent crude climbing above $95 per barrel, yet the impact on equities has been muted. Moreover, regulators in the United States and Europe have intensified scrutiny of AI safety, with several high‑profile incidents—ranging from biased algorithmic outputs to the misuse of deep‑fake technology—prompting calls for stricter oversight. Despite these warnings, the Nasdaq’s upward trajectory suggests that investors are betting on the sector’s growth potential outweighing short‑term regulatory headwinds.

Financial strategists point to a broader shift in risk appetite that has taken hold since the start of the year. The S&P 500’s technology weighting has risen to its highest proportion in a decade, reflecting a reallocation of capital from traditional value stocks toward firms perceived as future‑proof. “We’re seeing a classic ‘growth premium’ re‑emerge,” said Laura Chen, senior market analyst at Meridian Capital. “The market is pricing in a scenario where AI becomes a ubiquitous productivity engine, and that narrative is powerful enough to eclipse concerns about valuation multiples and geopolitical turbulence.” Chen added that the Nasdaq’s record level is also being buoyed by strong earnings reports from several mid‑cap AI players, which have consistently beaten consensus estimates and signaled accelerating revenue pipelines.

However, not all market participants share the same optimism. Some fund managers warn that the current rally could be a speculative bubble, citing historically high price‑to‑earnings ratios and the risk that AI adoption may take longer to materialize than investors anticipate. “If the AI hype cools or regulatory constraints tighten, we could see a sharp correction,” cautioned Raj Patel, portfolio manager at Horizon Equity. “The market is effectively betting on a future that is still uncertain, and any misstep—be it a major AI safety incident or a prolonged conflict in the Middle East—could trigger a rapid reassessment of risk.”

Looking ahead, the Nasdaq’s trajectory will likely hinge on how quickly AI technologies transition from experimental pilots to revenue‑generating products, and whether policymakers can devise frameworks that address safety without stifling innovation. In the short term, analysts expect the index to test the 15,600‑15,700 range, a level that would cement the rally as one of the most pronounced in recent memory. As the market continues to digest the dual forces of technological optimism and geopolitical tension, investors will be watching corporate earnings, regulatory developments, and the evolving dynamics of the US‑Iran conflict for clues on whether the AI‑driven ascent can sustain its momentum or will encounter a corrective pullback.
